summary: Geoffrey Samuel, a scholar of Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, earned his PhD at Cambridge under Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah, Peter J. Wilson, and Edmund Leach. He held posts at Lancaster, Newcastle, Sydney, and Cardiff, where he is Emeritus Professor.

Georg Buddruss (1929–2021) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the University of Tübingen and earned his Dr. phil. at Goethe University Frankfurt under Paul Thieme before serving as professor at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (1963–1995).

Georg Bühler (1837–1898) was an Indologist and linguist. He earned his PhD at Göttingen under Theodor Benfey and others. He held chairs at Elphinstone College and Bombay University (1863–1880) and later at the University of Vienna starting in 1880.

Georg Christoph Lichtenberg (1742–1799) was a German philosopher. He studied at the University of Göttingen from circa 1763 to 1769 and subsequently held a post there from around 1770 until his death in 1799.

Linguist Georg Curtius (1820–1885) studied at Bonn and Berlin under Bopp, Lassen, and others. He held professorships in classical philology at Charles University (1849–1854), Kiel University (1854–1862), and Leipzig University (1862–1885).

Georg Forster (1754–1794) was an Indologist who received early education at Saint Peter's School. He held academic posts at Vilnius University from 1784 to 1787 and at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz from circa 1788 to 1793.

Georg Friedrich Grotefend (1775–1853) was a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and history and archaeology. He was educated at Lessing-Gymnasium and studied at the University of Göttingen from circa 1795 to 1797.

Georg Huth (1867–1906) worked in Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at Leipzig University from circa 1885 to 1889 and held a post at Humboldt University of Berlin from around 1891 until 1906.

Georg Kaibel (1849–1901) was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. During his career, he held positions at the universities of Greifswald (~1879–1882), Rostock (~1882–1883), Breslau (~1883–1886), and Göttingen (~1897–1901).

Georg Ludolf Dissen (1784–1837) was a linguist who studied at the University of Göttingen (~1804–1808). He later held academic posts at the University of Marburg (~1812–1813) and the University of Göttingen (~1813–1837).

Georg Martin Dursch (1800–1881) was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at Tübingen and in Paris under Antoine-Léonard de Chézy. In 1829, he was appointed professor at Johann-Vanotti-Gymnasium Ehingen.

Georg Morgenstierne (1892–1978) was a linguist and scholar of Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Oslo, Bonn, and Berlin, he was a professor at Gothenburg (1930) and Oslo (1937–1962).
Georg Simmel (1858–1918) was a German philosopher. He completed his studies at the Humboldt University of Berlin circa 1876 to 1881 and subsequently held a post there from circa 1885 until 1914.

Georg Wilhelm Freytag (1788–1861) was a linguist who studied at Göttingen and under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy in Paris. He held a post at Königsberg and served as professor of oriental languages at Bonn from 1819 to 1861.

Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel (1770–1831) was a philosopher educated at the Tübinger Stift, Tübingen, and Jena under Schelling. He held positions at the University of Jena (~1801–1805), Heidelberg University (~1816–1818), and Frederick William University Berlin (~1818–1831).

Georg von Simson (born 1933) is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his doctorate and habilitation at Göttingen and worked at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (1968–1977) before serving as professor at Oslo (1977–2003).

Georg von der Gabelentz (1840–1893), a scholar of Sinology, linguistics, and Japanology, studied at Jena, Leipzig, and TU Dresden. He served as professor at Leipzig University (1878–1889) and Humboldt University of Berlin from 1889.

George A. Kennedy (1901–1960) was a linguist and sinologist who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1932–1935) under Erich Haenisch and Otto Franke. He subsequently held a post at Yale University from circa 1936 to 1960.

George A. Keyworth is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at UC Santa Barbara and earned his PhD from UCLA (2001) under Robert E. Buswell Jr., holding posts at Colorado (2001) and Saskatchewan (attested 2019).

George Abraham Grierson (1851–1941) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Trinity College Dublin. He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1871–1898) and was Superintendent of the Linguistic Survey of India from 1898 to 1928.
